title: Short Stuff: Lake Peigneur
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1980 Lake Peigneur disaster in Iberia Parish, Louisiana. Texico contractors drilling for gas in the lake accidentally broke into a salt mine beneath the lake, causing a large whirlpool that drew in the lake water, the nearby Gulf Intracoastal canal water, eleven barges, a tugboat, and a drilling platform into the mine. About fifty miners escaped by elevator, and no one died. The lake changed from freshwater to saltwater and from a few feet deep to about two feet, and Texico paid out millions in damages. The hosts attribute the error to a map-coordinate mix-up.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts open with light banter and introduce the Lake Peigneur story, a Louisiana lake that sits atop a salt dome.

segments.title: Drill rig stuck and sinking
segments.summary: In November 1980, Texico contractors drilling for gas in the shallow lake hit a stuck drill about 1,200 feet down. The rig tilted and sank, and the crew escaped on barges.

segments.title: Whirlpool forms and mine floods
segments.summary: The drill had broken into a salt mine shaft beneath the lake. A whirlpool grew to about a quarter mile across, and water flooded the mine, where an electrician sounded the alarm.

segments.title: Miners escape and lake drains into mine
segments.summary: About fifty miners rode elevators eight at a time to the surface. The whirlpool pulled in the Gulf of Mexico water via the canal, along with eleven barges, a tugboat, and a drilling platform. Air from the mine shot out as geysers.

segments.title: Aftermath and lasting changes
segments.summary: The water drained into the mine over hours, and most barges resurfaced. No one died. The lake became saltwater and about two feet deep. Texico paid millions in damages, and the error was blamed on mixed-up map coordinates.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts credit sources and sign off the Short Stuff segment.
